text:
julia: Quick heads-up — Acme Robotics agreed to a 4-week POC. Goal: integrate Redwood Private into their on-prem infra for assistant + retrieval reranker. Need an eval harness: golden dataset (~1k queries), scoring rubric, regression gates, and an execution timeline. Who can own what? cc @omar @maya

omar: Clarify success criteria: latency p99 < 250ms for generation endpoints, embedding recall@10 >= 0.90, and per-token cost target <= $0.02 (avg). Also need clear pass/fail gates for rollouts.

maya: For the golden set I suggest 6 intent buckets (domain queries, control commands, diagnostics, multi-step workflows, small-talk, error handling). 2 adversarial paraphrases each + 1 noisy input variant. That lands ~1k total. Include numeric precision checks and context carryover tests.

kevin: I can own the harness infra. Plan: Redwood Optimize + canary route to a dedicated pool. Need sample prompts, eval scripts, and storage for labeled golden answers. ETA: 2w to stand up harness infra, then 2w POC run.

security: Acme requires no customer data to leave their VPC. Private deployment + KMS keys & audit logs mandatory. I'll start filling the security questionnaire (encryption, access controls, data-at-rest/in-transit). Also want SOC2 addendum requested.

ryan: Infra note: we'll provision a dedicated pool (4x A100-equivalent) unless model size differs. Recommend pre-quantize to int8 to hit cost target; need confirmation on model family and sequence length distribution. We can set ephemeral KV cache to avoid persistent storage.

maya: Measurement plan: precision/recall per intent, NDCG for reranker, latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, and a hallucination heuristic tracked by simple QA checks + small hand-labeled set. Regression gate proposal: block rollout if recall drops >2% absolute or hallucination rate increases >10% relative.

alex: For scoring: use NDCG for reranking with golden relevance labels, exact-match or intent-class F1 for assistant responses. We'll need human labeling guidelines and an inter-annotator agreement target (kripp alpha >= 0.7). I'll prototype the label schema.

julia: Customer timeline: demo in 3 weeks, then 2-week POC run. Request: harness ready by demo week - 1 (so they can sanity-check). That means harness by 2026-05-03 if we target the demo week of May 10. Can we hit that?

kevin: Yes if we start today and get prompt sets from Acme + dedicated capacity approval. We'll parallelize infra & harness code.

omar: I'll handle contracting — pricing question from Acme: prefer 6mo committed capacity with monthly overage at 1.2x. Is that acceptable?

sara: Finance input: we can offer a 6-month commitment with overage at 1.25x. I'll prepare a simple term sheet and a non-binding quote.

security: Additional requirement from Acme: no logs persisted outside their VPC and customer-managed S3 for any artifacts. Also attestations for KMS key rotation policy.

ryan: We'll configure logging sinks to their S3 and ensure ephemeral caches. Need to confirm bandwidth and on-prem egress constraints.

maya: On prompts: include instruction-following permutations, temperature sweeps (0.0, 0.3, 0.7), and multi-turn history truncation tests. We'll capture stochastic variance and report confidence intervals.

alex: I'll draft an eval harness README and example scripts using the SDK + streaming. Will push a PR with a minimal `run_eval.sh` and `score.py` that computes NDCG and intent F1.

julia: Owners summary: kevin (harness infra), maya (eval design & prompt sets), alex (scripts + README), omar (contract/pricing), ryan (infra/deployment), sara (finance/term sheet), security (questionnaire & compliance). I'll schedule weekly syncs starting tomorrow. :calendar:

calendar-bot: Created event "Acme POC kickoff" for 2026-04-22 10:00 — attendees: julia, omar, kevin, maya, ryan, alex, sara, security

kevin: Next immediate actions: (1) maya to draft golden-set template + labeling guide by EOD Thu; (2) alex to open harness repo & example script by Mon; (3) omar to escalate contract and confirm committed capacity by EOD Fri. If any blockers call them out here.

maya: Will do the golden-set template. Also propose a small pilot dataset (100 queries) to sanity-check metrics before full run.

julia: Perfect. Thanks team — please drop any blockers here. :thumbsup:
